title: A word is dead
sub: Six short lines, and the whole poem turns in the middle. Some say a word dies the moment you say it — she says that is the day it starts living. Each level gives you a little less.

levels.name: Last words
levels.tag: One blank at the end of each line
levels.blurb: The whole poem is in front of you. Only the last word of each line is missing — and dead rhymes with said, say with day, so the rhymes will hand you most of them.

levels.name: First words
levels.tag: One blank at the start of each line
levels.blurb: Now the first word of each line is gone. Watch lines three and four: Some say, then I say. Those two words are the whole argument, and they are the ones people swap by accident.

levels.name: Half gone
levels.blurb: About half the words are away now. It is a short poem, so there is less to lean on here than there looks.

levels.name: Line by line
levels.blurb: One whole line at a time, with the rest of the poem still around it. Mind the commas: there is one after said, and a full stop after say.

levels.name: By heart
levels.blurb: No words on the screen at all. A picture for each line, and you say it out loud from memory — which is what you will be doing when you stand up.
